raw_response:
I am farming only 4.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly what has worked on my own land and what I see nearby people doing. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me. Wheat gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is not very good, I still have the other. Some people in the family work outside, so I cannot do anything too labor-heavy, and I also do not want to spend too much cash at once. I have well water, so if the weather turns dry I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times unless I have to. For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, use a common improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer before sowing, then add a little more at jointing if the crop looks weak. For maize, I will plant quickly after wheat harvest because the time is tight. I will not do complicated tillage, just a quick field preparation and sow. Maize usually responds well if I give enough base fertilizer and one topdress, so I will do that, but not too much because cash is tight. I will watch weeds and insects and spray only when I really see a problem.
